answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching vendors (memory_c2) carries unacceptable onboarding/integration risk under this timeline. Deferring is not viable since the contract doesn't auto-renew. The two most relevant precedents for meeting the 18% cost mandate without disrupting supply are renegotiating at renewal (memory_c4, recovered margin via benchmarking) and multi-year incumbent commitments unlocking volume pricing (memory_c6). Verifying these before committing lets me confirm whether benchmarked renegotiation or a longer-term commitment better meets the cost target without narrowing service or risking delivery continuity. Given the tight timeline, staying with the incumbent while aggressively renegotiating price/terms preserves delivery stability (no migration work, no interruption) while addressing the cost mandate, making negotiate_terms the safer, high-leverage action this cycle. Second-sourcing and full vendor switching remain queued for the next review cycle once verified.
